note: The children of Valentino Defranceschi and Helena/Elena, read out of the Liber Baptizatorum and the burial register of Fiume on 6 September 2026 and re-checked against the FamilySearch index on 20 September 2026. **Every child carries a `who` slug**, because an evidence file with no key to a person is an evidence file the build will drop — and this one was dropped for eleven days. The list stood at fourteen until the index turned up a fifteenth, **Jacobus Vincentius, baptised 21 July 1757**, whose entry was then read on the page. Eleven of the fifteen now carry the ark of the image they were read from.
heading: Valentino's fifteen children, out of the Fiume register
lead: Kobler's earliest Fiume household is «Valentino Defranceschi, venuto dalla Carnia, fu fatto Cittadino nel 1739». The register says what that citizenship was for: **he had been baptising children there since 1737**, and he went on doing it for twenty years. **Ten sons and five daughters** — and the tenth son only appeared on 20 September 2026. The family account has always said *ten sons*, and for as long as this archive had fourteen children it could only count nine. **With Jacobus Vincentius the sons come out at ten exactly.** Five of the fifteen are known only from the burial register.
source: Liber Baptizatorum and the burial register of the collegiate church of St Vitus, Fiume, read 6 September 2026; index arks recovered and three entries re-read on the page 20 September 2026. **Eleven of the fifteen now cite the image they stand on.** **The remaining four are exactly the four this archive had already named as being in no index** — *Ignatius Francus Mattheus 1745, Vitus Joannes Baptista 1751, Aloysius Rochus 1754 and Rosalia Francisca 1755* — which is a small vindication of the 6 September reading: everything it recorded that could be checked, checked out. Those four still exist only because the register itself was read, and need the film at their dates. *(doc for the eleven that cite an ark; doc — uncited for the four.)*
